title: Termwise coproducts in a Grothendieck derived category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be the localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every set $I$ in the chosen indexing universe and family of unbounded cochain complexes $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$, the termwise coproduct complex $(\bigoplus_iK_i)^r=\bigoplus_i K_i^r$, with differential induced by the $d_i^r$, exists. Its image $Q(\bigoplus_iK_i^\bullet)$, with the images of the termwise coprojections, is a coproduct of the $Q(K_i^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. The assertion includes the empty set.

proof.text: By [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], A has small colimits, hence each coproduct $S^r=\bigoplus_i K_i^r$ exists. With coprojections $j_i^r$, define $d_S^r$ by $d_S^r j_i^r=j_i^{r+1}d_i^r$. Testing on every coprojection gives $d_S^{r+1}d_S^r j_i^r= j_i^{r+2}d_i^{r+1}d_i^r=0$, so S is a cochain complex and the j_i are chain maps. Any family of chain maps $f_i:K_i\to T$ induces unique degreewise maps $f^r:S^r\to T^r$; their differential equations follow by testing on j_i. This proves the chain-level coproduct universal property.

Write $\mathsf K(A)$ for the homotopy category. Restriction gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf K(A)}(S,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf K(A)}(K_i,T)$ for every target complex T: choose chain representatives of the component classes and assemble them by Step 1 to prove surjectivity. For injectivity, if f and g have homotopic restrictions, choose component homotopies $h_i^r:K_i^r\to T^{r-1}$ and assemble $h^r:S^r\to T^{r-1}$. The equation $f^r-g^r=d_T^{r-1}h^r+h^{r+1}d_S^r$ holds on every j_i, hence holds globally. Conversely any homotopy restricts to the component homotopies. Thus the bijection is specifically restriction along the coprojections.

For an arbitrary derived object L choose a complex M representing it, as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] there is a quasi-isomorphism $M\to J$ with J K-injective, with no boundedness restriction. Localization turns this into an isomorphism $L\cong Q(J)$. Only existence and K-injectivity are used, not the functoriality clause.

Apply [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison] with target J and sources S and each K_i. It gives bijections from the homotopy-category Hom sets to the corresponding derived Hom sets. These commute with restriction along j_i because localization preserves composition. Conjugating the restriction bijection of Step 2 by these bijections gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q(S),Q(J))\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q(K_i),Q(J))$, and the resulting map is exactly restriction along Q(j_i).

source.place: Tag 07D9, displayed Hom calculation; derived.tex Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, assertion (3)

proof.text: Postcomposition with the isomorphism $L\cong Q(J)$ of Step 3 is bijective both on maps from Q(S) and on maps from every Q(K_i), and commutes with restriction along Q(j_i) by associativity. Therefore the restriction map into L is bijective as well. This is exactly the coproduct universal property for the specified Q(j_i). If I is empty, the degreewise coproducts in Step 1 are zero objects, there is a unique map from S into every T and the product of Hom sets in Steps 2 and 4 is a singleton. Hence the same proof covers the empty coproduct.
